nodes.label: Paddle Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: API_PADDLE, PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and PADDLE_ENV are server-only. Only VITE_-prefixed vars reach the frontend bundle, so an API key must never carry that prefix; VITE_PADDLE_CLIENT_TOKEN is public by design.

nodes.label: CloudCore Stack
nodes.rationale: SaaS panel for VPS infrastructure automation. NestJS 11 + TypeScript backend in src/, React 19 + Vite frontend in frontend/, PostgreSQL on Neon accessed with the pg driver directly (no ORM), app auth via JWT.

nodes.label: Content Security Policy
nodes.rationale: default-src 'self' with explicit allowances for https://*.paddle.com in script-src and frame-src. Without those entries initializePaddle() fails with 'Failed to load Paddle.js' and the checkout overlay never opens. frame-ancestors 'none' blocks clickjacking. Note script-src still permits 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval'.

nodes.label: SPA Mount Point
nodes.rationale: Single #root div with a module script loading /src/main.tsx — the Vite entry point for the whole React app.

nodes.label: Paddle Integration Policy
nodes.rationale: Paddle's API and SDKs change often, so the paddle-docs MCP must be consulted before writing integration code rather than trusting model knowledge. All development targets sandbox; sandbox API keys contain _sdbx and client tokens start with test_.

nodes.label: Secrets Committed To Git
nodes.rationale: Known outstanding risk: .env and .env.example are versioned in git with real credentials (Neon, SMTP, JWT, Paddle). No new secrets should be added to those files until they are removed from the repository.

nodes.label: Webhook Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Paddle retries webhook deliveries at-least-once, so handlers must deduplicate by event_id or the same event is processed twice.

nodes.label: Webhook Signature Verification
nodes.rationale: paddle.webhooks.unmarshal needs the RAW body. NestJS must be created with rawBody:true and read req.rawBody — if the body arrives already parsed as JSON the signature never validates.

nodes.label: SEO And Social Metadata
nodes.rationale: Open Graph and Twitter Card tags plus canonical https://cloudcore.lat/home. Positions CloudCore as a SaaS panel for VPS, WordPress, MySQL/PostgreSQL databases and SSH terminals. Authored by AbstracDev.

nodes.label: CloudCore Brand Palette
nodes.rationale: Four official colors: #005461 deep teal, #018790 mid teal, #00B7B5 vivid teal, #F4F4F4 light neutral. These are the source of the --brand-* CSS custom properties.

nodes.label: CoreBot Mascot (dark variant)
nodes.rationale: Same CoreBot mascot rendered on an opaque black background with a ground shadow. Hash-named and visually redundant with corebot.png; likely an unreferenced source asset rather than a used one.

nodes.label: CoreBot Head Crop
nodes.rationale: Square head-and-shoulders crop of the CoreBot mascot, sized for a small avatar slot. Used as the guide's face in the onboarding tour.

nodes.label: CoreBot Mascot (full body)
nodes.rationale: Cartoon robot mascot on transparent background: grey boxed head with large round eyes, orange antenna ball, magenta/pink accents on shoulders, hands and feet, striped articulated limbs. The pink and grey are off the documented brand palette — the mascot is a separate visual identity from the teal UI.

links.explanation: Visually identical solid teal/cyan cloud icon on transparent background, matching the root favicon.png asset - same asset duplicated in the frontend/public directory.
